history.summary: The Arulmigu Arudra Kabaliswarar Temple is an ancient Shiva temple in the heart of Erode city (Erode Fort area), and is NOT the famous Kapaleeswarar Temple of Mylapore, Chennai - a separate, well-attested Erode shrine. The identity is confirmed by multiple Erode-specific sources (erodeonline.in, velpu.com, TripAdvisor Erode listings) and an exact-address geocode (North Eswaran Kovil Street, Akilmedu Kottai, Erode Fort). Legend: a Chola ruler named Lakshmikanthan performed a yajna; pots of milk spilled at one spot, digging revealed blood oozing - a lingam struck by the crowbars, whose head (kabalam) broke into four pieces and flew to four places - hence the deity's name, Kabaleeswarar. A second legend tells of the poor weaver Thandavan: Shiva, disguised as a freezing old man, asked his wife for a cloth; when Thandavan obtained one from his employer and gave it, Shiva accepted it as his own parivattam - the cloth was found on the deity next morning, and Shiva possessed the village head's son to declare Thandavan innocent of its theft. The temple's specialties: 108 shivalingas carved on a single Shivalinga; sun worship - during the last days of Masi (Feb-Mar) the sun's rays penetrate the mandapams and fall on the Lord (claimed as the first such temple in Tamil Nadu - verify); epigraphy names the sthala Thondeeswaram and the Lord Thondeeswarar/Udaya Mahadeva/Thondargal Nayanar; 5-tier raja gopuram in Dravidian style; koneru (tank) called Changu theertham. Sage Durvasa is said to have installed Shiva here in Pallikonda (sayana) kolam, and the majority of devotees are from the weaving community. Dating is thin: velpu.com gives 1004-1280 AD, tamilnadu-favtourism links it to a Karikala of the Kongu Cholas, while travel sites call it '500 years old' or '1200 years old' (conflict - verify).

name: Arudra Kabaliswarar Temple
town_description: Erode is a major city of the Kongu Nadu region on the Kaveri river, a textile and turmeric trading hub. The Arudra Kabaliswarar Temple stands in the old Erode Fort area (North Eswaran Kovil Street), in the heart of the city - distinct from the Mylapore Kapaleeswarar Temple in Chennai with which the name could be confused.

travel.road: In the Erode Fort area, in the heart of Erode city (verify).
